solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Excellent prize fund, mine after retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the pair of words is read backwards

parts.note: a pot is a pool of prize money
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A miner's prize fund, collected after they retire, turns out to be excellent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after retirement' reverses the two pieces together, so the order of the parts flips as well as each word's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiptop is an informal adjective for first-rate, of the highest quality.

clue.text: Instant review of item impressing newspapers etc

indicators.note: to impress is to press into, so one piece is pushed inside the other
a review is a re-viewing, a looking over afresh, so the letters of the word are rearranged

parts.note: the media are newspapers, television and the like

explanation.surface: A quick review of an item that has impressed the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review of' rearranges the letters of item to IMTE, and 'impressing' presses the media piece into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate, as an adjective, means happening at once, the same as instant.

clue.text: Mass of grass beginning to smell like that, gather bundles up

indicators.note: to bundle up is to wrap around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: to tuck is to gather fabric into folds

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: so means in that way, like that

explanation.surface: Someone gathering bundles of grass that are starting to smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bundles up' is the containment signal: gather wraps around the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussock is a dense clump or tuft of growing grass.

clue.text: I should add one Greek character

parts.note: PS, postscript, is what a writer adds after signing off
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A writer adding a postscript to mention one Greek figure in the story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I should add' is the thought behind a postscript, PS, rather than a literal instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Psi is the twenty-third letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Impressive, refusing to work

explanation.surface: An impressive figure who nonetheless refuses to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one word: an adjective for impressive, and the participle of strike, to stop work in protest.

clue.text: Follow house guest part of the way?

indicators.note: only a part of the way through the words is taken, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: A house guest walking after the host for some of the journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To segue is to move smoothly on from one thing to the next, so to follow on.

clue.text: Legal victory over Germany for politician

parts.note: right, as in having a lawful title, can mean legal or just
a win is a victory

explanation.surface: A court victory over Germany making a politician's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A right-winger is a conservative member of a party, here a type of politician.

clue.text: A ruminant's heading off south of capital of Kenya, African city

indicators.note: in a down answer what is south of something comes below it, so after it
the capital, or head, of a word is its opening letter
with its heading, the first letter, taken away

parts.note: an impala is an African antelope, which chews the cud

explanation.surface: An antelope with its head down, grazing south of Kenya's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the antelope's first letter; 'south of' in a down clue means placed after the K.
explanation.definitionFit: Kampala is the capital of Uganda, a city in East Africa.

clue.text: Nine fish can swim freely with this?

definitions.meaning: a group of nine, especially musicians

definitions.text: fish can swim freely with this?
definitions.meaning: read as ..., the absence that leaves fish free

explanation.surface: A shoal of nine fish swimming freely.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into NO NET, which is why the question mark is there.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a set of nine, as a quartet is a set of four.

clue.text: Skill of tennis player, ace!

definitions.meaning: ..., hitting the ball hard downwards, is a tennis skill
ace and ... are both informal exclamations meaning excellent

explanation.surface: Praise for a tennis player's skill at serving an ace.
explanation.definitionFit: One word for a hard tennis stroke and British slang for wonderful or terrific.

clue.text: Willing to embrace popular tomboy

indicators.note: embracing is holding within the arms, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: game means up for it, willing
in means fashionable or popular

explanation.surface: A willing friend about to hug a popular tomboy.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamine is a slim girl with mischievous boyish charm, close to a tomboy.

clue.text: Around start of Oktoberfest the diet is going to pot — prompting help?

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed around the other piece
going to ruin, falling apart, so the letters are broken up and rearranged
the start of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Around Oktoberfest the diet collapses, and help is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going to pot' rearranges THE DIET IS, and 'Around' places it about the O from 'start of Oktoberfest'.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot sheet is a cue card held up off camera to prompt a television presenter with lines.

clue.text: Guard club, securing implement

parts.note: screw is slang for a prison warder
a driver is a golf club used off the tee

explanation.surface: A security guard carrying a club as a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guard' leads to the British slang screw, a prison officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwdriver is a hand tool used to drive in screws that fasten things.

clue.text: Book with info but no introduction

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter, which is left out

parts.note: facts are information

explanation.surface: A book full of information but lacking an introduction.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts, the Acts of the Apostles, is a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Second last place

definitions.meaning: to second a motion is to ... it, support it
the rear position, the last place

explanation.surface: Coming second, or finishing in last place.
explanation.definitionFit: Back as a verb means to support, like seconding, and as a noun the rearmost position.

clue.text: Regarding story about India — not finished yet?

parts.note: re means regarding, about

indicators.note: the story goes about, around, the letter for India

parts.note: a parable is a moral story
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Something said about a story about India that isn't finished yet.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is playful: something not yet finished, beyond repair, can still be fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A repairable item is not yet done for: it can still be mended and saved.

clue.text: Intimate, comfortable position set up

indicators.note: in a down answer, setting something up reads it upwards, so backwards

parts.note: sitting on someone's lap is a comfy place

explanation.surface: An intimate friend sets up a comfortable spot.
explanation.definitionFit: An intimate, as a noun, is a close friend, a pal.

clue.text: Visited by leader of gang, suspect not alone in Derbyshire town

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are visited, entered, by the other piece
suspect means doubtful, out of order, so the letters are rearranged
the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A suspect, not alone, visited by the head of a gang in a Derbyshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges NOT ALONE and 'Visited by' sets G, from 'leader of gang', inside. Derbyshire is an English county in the Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Long Eaton is a market town in south-east Derbyshire near Nottingham.

clue.text: Evidence of sickness in canary, weary

parts.note: canary yellow is a bright yellow colour
to flag is to tire, grow weary

explanation.surface: A sickly canary shows signs of illness and is weary.
explanation.definitionFit: A yellow flag flown by a ship signals disease aboard, or a request for quarantine clearance.

clue.text: Breach of trust by British country

indicators.note: a breach is a break in something, so another piece breaks into it

parts.note: to lean on someone is to rely on, trust them

explanation.surface: A British country accused of breach of trust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breach of' breaks LEAN ON open with B.
explanation.definitionFit: Lebanon is a country on the eastern Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: Figure 101 suggested?

parts.note: 101 is shown as C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, followed by ONE

explanation.surface: A figure of 101 is put forward.
explanation.walkthrough: The number is read as a hundred, C in Roman numerals, followed by the word ONE for the final 1.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone is a solid geometric shape, a figure in mathematics.

clue.text: Cooler book from Poe, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a spine-chilling story, like Edgar Allan Poe's tales

explanation.surface: Something cooler, a tale from Poe perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigerating device and a frightening horror story share the one word.

clue.text: Finish off sweet, mint?

indicators.note: the finish of the word, its last letter, is taken off

parts.note: a bombe is a dome-shaped frozen dessert, a sweet

explanation.surface: Finishing off a sweet, perhaps a mint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mint' looks like a sweet; it means a fortune. In Britain a bomb is a large sum of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A mint and a bomb are both informal words for a very large amount of money.

clue.text: Old and wise, native American

parts.note: sage means wise

explanation.surface: An old, wise Native American elder.
explanation.definitionFit: The Osage are a Native American people of the Great Plains, now in Oklahoma.

clue.text: Others came down in chains

parts.note: the rest are the others
it rained, came down from the sky

explanation.surface: Other people were brought down in chains.
explanation.definitionFit: Restrained means held back by force, as someone in chains is.

clue.text: Laid before heart, spades accumulate points?

indicators.note: one piece is laid before the other, so it comes first

parts.note: S is the card-game abbreviation for spades
the core is the heart of something

explanation.surface: In a card game, spades laid before a heart to rack up points.
explanation.definitionFit: To score is to gain points in a game, building up a tally.

clue.text: Route finder took position before vehicle sent the wrong way

indicators.note: the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: sat means took a seat, a position

indicators.note: sent in the wrong direction, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A route finder takes up position before a vehicle and sends it the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent the wrong way' turns VAN into NAV.
explanation.definitionFit: A satnav, satellite navigation device, plans routes for drivers.

clue.text: Line in bootees unfortunately no longer in use

indicators.note: the letter for line is set within the other piece
something that has gone wrong, unluckily, has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A line of baby bootees that unfortunately are no longer in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges BOOTEES, and 'in' puts L into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsolete means out of date, no longer used.

clue.text: Loan shark, unspeakable blackguard first of all

indicators.note: the first letter of each of all the words is taken

explanation.surface: A loan shark is an unspeakable villain, above all.
explanation.definitionFit: A sub is an advance of money, a small loan, in British informal use.

clue.text: Baby feeder exciting wee runts

indicators.note: exciting stirs things up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone who feeds babies exciting the tiny runts.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet nurse is a woman employed to breastfeed another's baby.

clue.text: Pedestrian operating drill

definitions.meaning: pedestrian as an adjective means dull
a drill operating is ... a hole

explanation.surface: A dull pedestrian using a drill.
explanation.definitionFit: Boring means tedious, and is also the present participle of bore, to drill.
